title: Street Oceanography
summary: Streets as open systems read as a sea: the tide of their walkers, its currents and surges, the waves of a crowd, how a street answers the weather and the calendar, how its uses mix and work together.

layers.title: the tide on the streets
layers.about: Each sensor's street as a channel of water standing to the level of its walkers (a metre for every hundred an hour): the tide the calendars predict at the clock's hour, the count observed on the date and its surge, the time of high water, the kind of tide.

layers.title: currents: walkers each way
layers.about: The walkers each way past the sensors that count each way, as many as walk there on average at the clock's hour, moving in real time; their colour toward or away from the centre of the counts; the net current as an arrow.

layers.title: waves on Swanston Street (a model)
layers.about: The crowd walking north from Flinders Street as a kinematic wave, second by second: its blocks and cross streets from the map, signals at the streets, walkers entering at the counted rate, queues spilling back from red crossings.

layers.title: pedestrians at the sensors, by hour
layers.about: Columns at Melbourne's pedestrian sensors, their height the mean count at the clock's hour of the week (2024–2026).

layers.title: shops and services, open or closed
layers.about: Holdings along the named streets, coloured by use; those open at the clock's hour stand tall.

layers.title: businesses by use (land-use census)
layers.about: Every business about the sensors in the City of Melbourne's census of land use, coloured by use.

tools.title: Tides and currents of the city
tools.about: Every street's tide and current together: when the city's high water comes, which streets have two crests a day, the commuters' flood and ebb, the arrow of time on the streets, which way walkers keep, and the surge on a date.

tools.title: Rhythm of a street
tools.about: A sensor's counts read on the week, the month and the year: spectrum, harmonic constants, whose clock the street keeps.

tools.title: Weather and holidays
tools.about: How much rain, heat and holidays change a street's counts, and every street side by side.

tools.title: Mix of uses
tools.about: The uses along a street or about a sensor: how far they mix, at what scale, and over the years.

tools.title: Opening hours
tools.about: Where and when a street is open, the rhythm of its hours, and which kinds of people its open shops draw.

tools.title: Stores that work together
tools.about: Which uses keep company; two stores as a pathway in space and time, its visitors spreading along the street on the map; the spacing of clusters.

tools.title: Crowds and circulation
tools.about: Swanston Street's crowd through the day as a kinematic wave, with its carriageway opened or not; movement round the blocks of a district.

tools.title: Kinds of streets
tools.about: Melbourne's streets placed by how finely their uses change and how selectively they answer the calendar.

source: Wanhong Huang, Street Oceanography (working paper, 2026), and its companion case study; the urban-science domain's theory/street-oceanography.md
